title: Barnes's advice on seasoned musicians and four-beat drumming
summary: Reason relays Barnes's advice to hire seasoned players and criticizes younger drummers who play two beats to the bar.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: And then I also took the bass player from Harry Walker's band. His name was Louis Matthews, an old man. I wanted all the guys. Now, this is the information what Paul Lee Barnes gave me, the advice. Years ago, he said, if you ever have a band and you want to play, keep this, your style's going to get some seasoned musicians.

That's going to back you up instead of them trying to back themselves up. And he said, you'll find a lot of flash through the younger musicians, but they won't play what you want them to play. Mm-hmm. And during that time, so many bands, young musicians began to stretch out from Dixieland. See? They would just like a takeoff from it. They'd play everything. But basically, they had to come right back to Dixieland because the beat had to be there. But then they, when we were playing four beats to the measure, a lot of the boys, the younger ones, who didn't have that good foot, like Freddie Coleman or Louis and Paul Barber and them, I could play that four beats to the measure like that. Well, they began to play two and make it up with their hands. Mm-hmm. Well, in one way, it's an easier way to play. Easier way the whole time. And, but it's a lazy way of playing. And fellas like Freddie Coleman and Louis and so many other good drummers. One of this guy, Alonzo Stewart. Mm-hmm. He came along a little bit afterwards, but he came along with that full beat.
